The performance of ECCOsorb-T1 measured from the laboratory testing was used in the TEA analysis. Structured Sorbent Concept, Validation, and Manufacturing As summarized in the initial TEA, to reduce the cost of CO removal, the structured sorbent assembly must 2 achieve a low cost of manufacturing, high sorbent loading capacity, low pressure drop with high air throughput, capable of direct joule heated regeneration, and can utilize existing manufacturing infrastructures. With this goal, Susteon developed a coated filter concept as the structured sorbent. The coated filter consists of the sorbent sandwiched between two filter layers, where one layer is electrically conductive and can be Joule heated. The sorbent coating onto the surface of the nonwoven filter substrate allows for high sorbent loading, up to 90% by weight, compared to <50wt% in monolith-based substrates. This sandwiched structured sorbent can then be pleated and framed, providing more surface area along a 3- dimensional plane. Once framed, the pleated filter panel can be arranged in a V-shape to represent one structured sorbent module. Susteon initiated a joint development agreement with a commercial partner, a global leader in air filtration, to assess the feasibility of manufacturing the structured sorbent filters at an industrial scale using the commercial partner’s existing filter manufacturing infrastructure. Specifically, the commercial partner agreed to manufacture the structured sorbent filters using an existing pilot manufacturing line. The manufactured structured sorbent filters were then tested in Susteon’s bench-scale DAC system as discussed below. To prepare the filter panels, the following activities were completed: 1. Select and verify the sustained performance of the electrically conductive nonwoven substrate for using in the structured sorbent filter 2. Manufacture samples of sorbent coated filters to test their performance in terms of sustained Joule heating cycles and CO adsorption/desorption capability 2 3.
